# Before the workshop

Complete this page before the session. The workshop starts from a working
installation rather than spending teaching time on downloads.

## Install the tools

You need:

1. **Quarto {{< var workshop.quarto-version >}}** from
   [quarto.org](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/).
2. **R 4.3 or later** from [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/).
3. An editor with Quarto support: RStudio, Positron, or VS Code.
4. A LaTeX installation for PDF. TinyTeX is the smallest supported route for
   most participants.

If you do not already have TinyTeX, run this once in R:

```r
install.packages("tinytex")
tinytex::install_tinytex()
```

Restart your editor after installing Quarto or TinyTeX.

## Prepare the project

1. Download the [starter
   project](materials/downloads/quarto-workshop-starter.zip).
2. Extract it to a short, writable path.
3. Open the extracted folder as an RStudio/Positron/VS Code project or workspace.
4. Open a terminal **inside that folder**.

Do not work inside the zip file, a mail attachment preview, or a temporary
downloads viewer.

## Install the R packages

From the project terminal, run:

```bash
Rscript setup.R
```

This installs only packages that are missing: `knitr`, `rmarkdown`, `readr`,
`dplyr`, and `ggplot2`.

## Run the preflight

```bash
Rscript preflight.R
```

The check reports:

- Quarto and R versions;
- required R packages;
- a detected LaTeX engine; and
- whether a tiny HTML and PDF document can render.

::: {.checkpoint}
### Checkpoint <span class="time">before arrival</span>

The final line reads `Preflight passed`. If HTML works but PDF fails, follow the
[PDF troubleshooting steps](appendices/troubleshooting.qmd#pdf-will-not-render)
before the workshop.
:::

## Make the first render

```bash
quarto render manuscript.qmd --to html
```

Open `manuscript.html`. It will be incomplete—that is intentional—but it should
contain a title, introduction, and activity placeholders.

::: {.callout-note}
You can use your editor's **Render** button instead of the terminal. The workshop
shows terminal commands because they behave consistently across editors.
:::

## Bring on the day

- the extracted starter project;
- the completed preflight result; and
- your laptop and power adapter
